description: Library L11 (P5+P2). Rear-end collision two weeks after an annual primary-care visit that lists two earlier car accidents, a chronic low back problem and a baseline back pain score. Attorney-referred spine clinic under a letter of protection, a scanned intake form (OCR text) answering 'prior accidents: No', and an itemized ledger with charges, a payment, a courtesy adjustment and a balance. Only stated charges count; payment, adjustment and balance are listed unclear.

totals.accept_all_reason: Hand-verified against the records: ED charge $3,260 + ledger lines $250 + $180 + $2,310 = $6,000; the $2,740 ledger total, $300 payment, -$274 adjustment and $2,166 balance are never charges. D-060 (default-deny): the three ledger lines (new patient exam, x-ray, treatment visits 1 through 14) state no date of service, so they are not itemized service lines and are listed under Amounts not totaled. Accepting the acceptable lines one at a time gives $3,260.00 (the ED charge); $6,000.00 is reached after the paralegal reads the ledger and reclassifies the three lines.

flags.summary: Treatment gap of 35 days (2026-04-24 to 2026-05-29), longer than 30.
Problem list entry before the collision; stated as the record's wording only.
Two earlier car accidents reported by the patient in a note dated two weeks before the collision.
Back pain score recorded before the collision.

The intake form answers 'Prior accidents? No' while the primary-care note of 2026-03-04 lists accidents in 2019 and 2022. Both cited; the tool does not say which is right. T-141: the code reads a checked 'No [X]' (OCR 'No IX]') as the denial and an accident named by a year before the form's year as a prior event, so this pair is now proposed and sent to the judge.
Attorney referral and letter-of-protection treatment (internal notes only, D-001/D-018); the record wording is stated and no inference is drawn about charges.

must_not_flag.statement: No gap flag for the 14, 9 and 28-day intervals; the letter of protection (record 4) and the ledger (record 9) are not gap endpoints.

No 'stated accident date is later than the first recorded treatment' conflict. The earliest record (2026-03-04, record 1) is an annual primary-care visit two weeks BEFORE the collision; the stated date 2026-03-18 (record 4, letter of protection) is the date of the EMS and ED records (2, 3) and no earlier record describes this collision (T-141, GATE-M2 paralegal major).

evidence.excerpt: Problem list: hypertension, type 2 diabetes, chronic low back pain.

tolerated.summary: A second form field ('Prior injuries?' answered No) paired with a different sentence of the same primary-care note. The code proposes one pair per denial and prior sentence; the judge classifies each and the first confirmed pair per denial stands (T-141).

must_not.statement: Counts the ledger total, payment, adjustment or balance as a charge, or adds the total line to the lines (values 2,740 / 2,166 / 274 / 300 / 8,740).
Nets the payment or adjustment into the billed figure, calls the charges reduced, reasonable or inflated, or states what was incurred.
bad_examples: Charges after the courtesy discount total $5,726.
The clinic reduced its bill to $2,166.00.
good_examples: Ledger lists total charges $2,740.00, payment $300.00, a courtesy discount and a balance due; none netted.
Billed charges accepted from these records: $6,000.00.
Account held under letter of protection.

must_not.statement: Calls the intake answer false or dishonest (lied, false, misrepresented).
bad_examples: She lied on the intake form.
good_examples: Intake form answer: Prior accidents? No.
The 2026-03-04 note lists car accidents in 2019 and 2022, per patient.
Intake and primary-care note differ; both cited.

must_not.statement: Decides the neck or back complaints are pre-existing, old, or not caused by the collision, or apportions between the earlier accidents and this one.
bad_examples: Her back pain predates the collision.
Most of the low back pain is from the 2022 accident.
The collision did not cause her low back pain.
good_examples: Chronic low back pain is on the 2026-03-04 problem list.
History per patient: car accidents in 2019 and 2022 with neck and low back pain.

notes: Library packet (T-079); scenario shapes: P5 + P2 in research/case-library-sources-v2.md; layouts in research/record-formats.md. All names, providers, places, dates and amounts are invented.

Hand arithmetic (encounters): 03-04 to 03-18 = 14; 03-18 to 03-27 = 9 (records 5 and 6 share 03-27); 03-27 to 04-24 = 4 + 24 = 28; 04-24 to 05-29 = 6 + 29 = 35 (flag). The LOP letter (03-26) and the ledger (06-15) are non-encounters.

Older notes come from the firm's records request to the PCP; the intake form is the clinic's. D-042 calibrated confidence: the tool shows measured precision per state for the pre-existing flags, never an invented percentage.
Ledger columns follow P5's billing items 1-4 and 6 (billed, adjustment, payment, balance, LOP); the carrier-contract item is a separate document and is not in this packet.
